name: sbt artifacts
auth: READ permission is required to resolve metadata and bytes; DEPLOY is additionally required to publish. Supply an unexpired Access token in AW_TOKEN; Basic authentication uses AW_USER matching the token subject. Token scope must retain the repository permissions; a token cannot grant access that its principal lacks.
fresh_home: Use a new project directory and separate Java user home, sbt global/Ivy directories and COURSIER_CACHE for each consumer. The acceptance image shares only pinned sbt bootstrap artifacts; the controlled dependency must be fetched from the selected repository.
prerequisites: Existing sbt repository and the pinned sbt launcher.
The example uses Maven-compatible publication layout. Build plugin cross-version and arbitrary custom Ivy layouts are separate contracts.
Run sbt from a directory containing project/build.properties with sbt.version=2.0.12.

configure.code:
umask 077
AW_WORK=$(mktemp -d)
export COURSIER_CACHE="$AW_WORK/coursier"
export AW_REPOSITORY_URL="$AW_URL/artifactory/$AW_REPO"
export AW_URL AW_USER AW_TOKEN
AW_HOST=$(python3 -c 'import os, urllib.parse; print(urllib.parse.urlsplit(os.environ["AW_URL"]).hostname)')
export AW_HOST
export SBT_OPTS="-Duser.home=$AW_WORK/home -Dsbt.global.base=$AW_WORK/global -Dsbt.ivy.home=$AW_WORK/ivy"
configure.note: AW_HOST is the hostname without port for the Basic authentication realm. AW_URL must be exported before this setup.

configure.code:
organization := "org.weave.recipe"
version := "1.0.0"
autoScalaLibrary := false
crossPaths := false
credentials += Credentials("Artifactory Realm", sys.env("AW_HOST"), sys.env("AW_USER"), sys.env("AW_TOKEN"))
resolvers := Seq("artifactweave" at sys.env("AW_REPOSITORY_URL"))
externalResolvers := resolvers.value
configure.note: Common build.sbt settings for the small Java/ordinary JAR example. Use HTTPS in production. CI explicitly permits HTTP only for its loopback fixture.

publish.note: Add these producer settings and run from the producer project. The dependency bytes are published by sbt itself.

steps.code:
name := "widget"
publishTo := Some("artifactweave" at sys.env("AW_REPOSITORY_URL"))
Compile / packageDoc / publishArtifact := false
Compile / packageSrc / publishArtifact := false
steps.note: Append to producer build.sbt; create src/main/resources/payload.txt containing the bytes to publish.

install.note: Use a separate consumer project and a fresh home/cache. Append the dependency settings to the common build.sbt.

steps.note: consumer/build.sbt; % deliberately avoids Scala cross-version suffixes.

limitations: The native proof covers local and one-node federated publication plus local, remote-cache and virtual resolution, including bad credentials. It does not claim every sbt plugin layout.
Remote and virtual publication is omitted; publish to the selected concrete deployment repository.
--server keeps this one-shot invocation in the foreground rather than leaving an sbt server process attached to a user home.

contains: sbt publishes and resolves through a <class> repository
